# The three-valued X < Y of balls, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_less_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The three-valued answer to whether $x < y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, $X$ and $Y$ not being empty, $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$: *yes* only if it holds for every choice of members, *no* only if it fails for every choice, otherwise *unknown*, both masks false:

$$\mathit{yes} \implies X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x < y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y, \qquad \mathit{no} \implies X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x < y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `less(X, Y)` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Trit` | `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |
| `greater(Y, X)` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Trit` | the operands exchanged; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{yes}$ is true only if $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x < y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; $\mathit{no}$ only if $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x < y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; never both. Both false is the answer *unknown*.
- An empty operand gives *unknown*, and so does the whole line.
- When an operand is the empty set or the whole line, the answer is exact: each mask is true exactly when its relation holds.
- When every operand is finite (a finite ball) and $\lvert r_x + r_y\rvert \le \Omega$, the answer is exact as well.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_less_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallPredicates.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_less_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_less_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the sum of the radii and the differences of the centers as exact pairs, compared (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_less_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_less_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum_ord`](two_sum_ord.md), [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md), [`le_2_2`](le_2_2.md).

```
# The three-valued X < Y of balls with one-limb centers (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface",
# "Comparisons"): yes when every member of X is below every member of Y, c_x + r_x < c_y - r_y, that
# is r_x + r_y < c_y - c_x, decided exactly on the exact pairs two_sum_ord(r_x, r_y) and
# two_sum_ord(c_y, -c_x) by lt_2_2; no when none is, r_x + r_y <= c_x - c_y, by le_2_2 and a test
# that the sum of the radii is finite (two sums that overflow are both (+inf, -inf), which le_2_2
# calls equal). Both false for an empty operand and for the whole line, through the same operations.
# Exact unless the sum of the radii and the difference of the centers both overflow; the claim says
# the half that a condition can: exact when r_x + r_y <= Omega.

(s0, s1) = two_sum_ord(rx, ry)
ncx      = neg(cx)
(d0, d1) = two_sum_ord(cy, ncx)
ncy      = neg(cy)
(g0, g1) = two_sum_ord(cx, ncy)
yes      = lt_2_2(s0, s1, d0, d1)
b        = le_2_2(s0, s1, g0, g1)
sa       = abs(s0)
fs       = lt(sa, const inf)
no       = and(b, fs)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_less_1)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 3 domains of 3 formats | 3 420 868 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
